title: Spleen removal (splenectomy)
what: The surgeon removes the spleen, usually through a few small openings, sometimes through a cut. Other organs partly take over its work.
why: For a ruptured spleen after an injury, some blood disorders, cysts, or tumors.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 3 hours, with 2 to 7 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Blood disorders and your platelet count
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Vaccines
prepare.text: For planned surgery, vaccines against pneumococcus, meningococcus, and Hib are usually given in advance.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

steps: You change, and an IV line is placed
The surgeon makes small openings or a cut on the left side of the belly
The spleen's blood vessels are tied off, and the organ is removed
The wound is stitched. Sometimes a drain is placed
feel: Pain in the left side. You will get painkillers
Sometimes shoulder pain from the gas. It passes in 1 to 2 days
after: You start getting up and walking early
No heavy lifting for a few weeks
Without a spleen, infections can be more serious. With a fever, see a doctor right away
Tell every doctor that you have no spleen
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F): get help right away. Do not wait
Severe belly pain, weakness, or paleness
Calf pain, shortness of breath, or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: How do I live without a spleen?
faq.a: Usually normally. Get your vaccines, and do not wait out a fever. See a doctor right away.

faq.q: Do I need vaccines after surgery?
faq.a: Yes, on your doctor's schedule. They are repeated after a few years.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Bring your test results and vaccination record. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
